article_title: OCaml 5.5.2 Fixes Six OSEC Advisories, Including Marshal Demarshaling and Windows Command Quoting; Each Advisory Credits Anthropic as Reporter

content_preview.title: OCaml 5.5.2 Fixes Six OSEC Advisories, Including Marshal Demarshaling and Windows Command Quoting; Each Advisory Credits Anthropic as Reporter
content_preview.summary: OCaml 5.5.2, tagged October 23, 2026, fixes six OSEC advisories in Str, Unix.map_file, Marshal, Windows command quoting and runtime_events, plus four other bugs including two miscompilations.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The OCaml project tagged patch release 5.5.2 on October 23, 2026, according to the [GitHub release page](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/releases/tag/5.5.2). The release notes say it contains several security fixes, identified as OSEC-2026-21 through OSEC-2026-26, and four other bug fixes: two miscompilations, a macOS configuration fix and a runtime events library fix. The OCaml security advisory database credits Anthropic as the reporter on each of the six advisories, for example in...

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise, well-structured Briefing (603 words, within the 300-800 range): overview, one bullet per advisory, other fixes, and a 'What We Don't Know' section. Technical detail is accurate and proportionate. Title is 142 characters (under the 150 limit). Internal link to the earlier curl article uses the correct singular /article/ form and the target exists (2026-10/15-curl-8230-...). Human-requested: false.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 sources are first-party OCaml project pages on github.com (release page, Changes file on the 5.5 branch, six advisory files in ocaml/security-advisories); the article states 'This briefing cites only first-party OCaml project pages', which is accurate and disclosed. github.com is on the allowlist. All 8 snapshots (source-0..7.html.gz in sources/2026-11/ocaml-552-.../) fetched with HTTP 200, sha256 re-computed on the decompressed content and matched the manifest, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all. I read the rendered snapshots for the credits check and read the raw text of every file (raw.githubusercontent.com for the six advisories and the Changes file; GitHub releases API/page for the release) for claim-by-claim verification. source-0 (release page): release 'OCaml 5.5.2', published_at 2026-10-23T12:35:53Z (created 11:54Z), not a prerelease; body lists security fixes OSEC-2026-21..26 and 'four other safe and useful bugfixes' = two miscompilations (atomic loads, immediate range patterns), macOS configuration, runtime events infinite loop; this confirms the article's 'four other bug fixes' sentence. The release date of October 23, 2026 is confirmed by the release page; the git tag object itself could not be queried (API rate limit), so 'tagged October 23' rests on the release creation/publish date, which is a minor caveat. source-1 (Changes, 5.5.2 section): independently recounted the entries without an OSEC identifier: #15045 atomic loads DCE, #15067/#15071 macOS detection, #15043/#15076 runtime events infinite loop (user event larger than half the ring buffer), #15185/#15187 pattern-matching miscompilation on immediate ranges and redundant patterns = 4, matching the release notes; 'two miscompilations' is the release notes' own characterisation (the Changes file labels only the pattern-matching one as a miscompilation), so it is the project's count, attributed in the article to the release notes in the Overview and used in the summary as a plain count. The six OSEC-tagged entries match the advisory set. source-2 OSEC-2026-21: Str.string_partial_match stale capture registers underflow, beginning > end, Str.replace_matched can crash (memcpy end-beginning), 5.5 (Medium), CWE-122, affected-conditions text as described, timeline 2026-08-24 / 2026-08-27 / 2026-09-29: all confirmed. source-3 OSEC-2026-22: Unix.map_file integer overflow in dimension product, caml_umul_overflow raising Failure, negative positions raise Invalid_argument, 5.5 (Medium), CWE-190: confirmed; same timeline confirmed. source-4 OSEC-2026-23: multiple Marshal issues, bindings from_channel/from_bytes/from_string/input_value, score 6.8, alias CVE-2026-28364, 'followup for OSEC-2026-01', 'Marshal is not type safe', 'recommended to use Marshal only for communication between trusted processes'; same timeline: confirmed. source-5 OSEC-2026-24: 7.3 (High), CVE-2026-41083, CWE-78, Filename.quote_command characters not properly escaped on Windows, Unix.create_process* raises Failure for .bat/.cmd arguments that cannot be securely passed: confirmed. source-6 OSEC-2026-25: heap buffer overflow heading, runtime_events consumer / oversized custom user event, 4.5 (Medium), fix 'Check message lengths for all runtime event types, report a corrupt stream on mismatch', affected setup 'producer and consumer run in separate processes, and the producer can be tricked into producing malformed data': confirmed. source-7 OSEC-2026-26: 4.5 (Medium), 'Validate event type against expected type, report a corrupt stream on mismatch', same affected-setup text: confirmed. Reporter credit: every one of the six advisory files contains the exact line [reporter "Anthropic"] in its credits block (alongside coordinators Hannes Mehnert and Edwin Török), and each carries an ANT-2026-xxxxxxxx identifier. The title phrase 'Each Advisory Credits Anthropic as Reporter' is therefore accurate and is phrased as the advisories state it. Merge-date omission: the timelines of -24 (2029-09-05), -25 (2027-09-05) and -26 (2027-10-20) carry impossible future years while -21/-22/-23 say 2026-09-29; the article correctly omits those three dates and says the year appears to be a typographical error, which is a fair, neutral characterisation. 'What We Don't Know' claims (advisories do not say how issues were found, do not say whether exploited) hold for all six advisory files. 'Internal ANT-2026 report identifiers' is the writer's characterisation of the ANT-2026-* IDs; the advisories do not call them internal, a trivial gloss. Cross-source nuance: the Changes file credits 'report by Hannes Mehnert' for OSEC-2026-25 and -26 (and no reporter for the others), while the advisories list Anthropic as reporter and Mehnert as coordinator; the article relies on and explicitly attributes the credit to the advisory database, so it is accurate, but the divergence is not mentioned.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, version, score, CVE alias, CWE, function name and quoted term (the only quoted string is "Anthropic") was checked against the raw source text and holds. No fabricated or unsourced specifics found. No bidirectional source gap: every body URL is in article.sources and vice versa (the only extra link is the internal curl article). Version/date: tagged/released 2026-10-23 (published 12:35 UTC), advisories published 2026-10-23 22:30 +01:00 per their frontmatter.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive. No alarmism about exploitability; scores and affected-condition caveats are reproduced as the advisories state them. The disclosure sentence 'The Herald's contributor model is also built by Anthropic' is accurate (contributor_model is Claude Sonnet 5.5, an Anthropic model), factual, and neutral; it appears in the Overview where the Anthropic credit is introduced, which is the right place. It is not AI self-reference in the prohibited sense and it declares a relevant interest.
editor_notes.originality: No existing OCaml coverage in src/content/articles. The only related piece is the 2026-10-15 curl 8.23.0 article (Anthropic-credited fix), correctly linked as prior coverage rather than duplicated. New topic.
concerns: The article is published about 11 days after the 2026-10-23 release; the advisories were modified on 2026-10-26 (OSEC-21) and 2026-10-28 (OSEC-25/26). Recency/news value is reduced but the consolidated six-advisory view and the Anthropic-credit angle are still new to the Herald archive.

The Changes file credits Hannes Mehnert as 'report by' for OSEC-2026-25 and -26, whereas the advisories list Anthropic as reporter and Mehnert as coordinator. Not an error in the article (it attributes the credit to the advisories) but the divergence is unreported.
'tagged October 23, 2026' is supported by the release page publication date; the tag object date was not independently queryable.

Source concentration: all 8 sources are first-party OCaml project pages, so no independent corroboration of the Anthropic credit exists; acceptable for a Briefing about what the project's own advisories say, and the article discloses it.
recommendations: Future OCaml coverage could note the Changes file versus advisory reporter-credit difference for OSEC-2026-25/-26.
Consider calling the ANT-2026 identifiers 'report identifiers' without 'internal' unless a source says so.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, neutrally worded, fully source-backed Briefing on a security patch release of a niche-but-important language toolchain, with a transparent first-party-only and contributor-model disclosure. Title, summary and lead are each supported by cited sources; no corrections required. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate security-release coverage for OCaml users with a modest Anthropic-reporter angle, but incremental and first-party-sourced only
